artifact.name: github-pages

failure_policy.auth_401_403: once start may have entered, authentication or authorization rejection is outcome-uncertain and is reconciled under the same deterministic operation ID; it never authorizes another start
failure_policy.rate_limit_403_429: once start may have entered, 403/429 is outcome-uncertain; Retry-After is diagnostic only because mutation is never started again
failure_policy.provider_error_protocol: PagesProviderError strict discriminated class including transport; no adapter-supplied post-start ambiguity flag
failure_policy.post_start_uncertainty: every start return, rejection, timeout, transport error, 4xx, 5xx, or unknown result enters operation read-back under the already-established aggregate absolute deadline; remaining time is recomputed before every readOperation, readback, and delay, each call timeout is min(request_timeout_ms, remaining), no call starts at zero remaining, exact terminal success deploys, otherwise the lifecycle returns pending/unknown and preserves the operation claim
failure_policy.idempotency: one deterministic operation, claim, and idempotency identity is derived by the lifecycle from candidate plus expected active; the provider's atomic durable claim is the sole admission authority, start is called at most once, and every resume polls that same provider-visible operation
failure_policy.stale_and_concurrent: reject generations not newer than active, retained, in-progress release, and expected-active history; when validating an exact pending candidate, exclude only that exact identity from the generation maximum and evaluate every other history item; any different in-progress operation blocks a new deployment
failure_policy.readback_schema: safeReadback recursively rejects root, nested-object, and array Proxy nodes with node:util/types.isProxy before prototype, descriptor, symbol, key, or value reflection on that node, then clones only recursively plain own-enumerable data-property graphs and validates exact active, inProgress, and retained keys; identity collision checks include active, retained, inProgress.release, and inProgress.expectedActive
failure_policy.test_harness_boundary: Production safeReadback, runBoundedPagesDeployment, and rollbackPagesDeployment always use this canonical policy and reject caller policy arguments. The scripted adapter exists only under tests/support; accelerated policy is accepted only by deep-module functions explicitly named ForTest, never by pages-deployment-contract.mjs.
failure_policy.start_atomicity: provider claim(operation, options) atomically persists the deterministic operation, expected-active CAS, and provider-visible pending claim before any remote mutation; only the caller receiving exact disposition acquired may call start
failure_policy.durable_claim: claim returns exact disposition acquired only to the first caller and exact disposition exists to all later, concurrent, or resumed callers for that operation; an unknown return, timeout, or error never authorizes start and can only reconcile the deterministic operation
failure_policy.claim_crash_recovery: a crash after claim but before start may leave a permanent pending claim requiring manual adjudication; the lifecycle must never resend start for that operation
failure_policy.aggregate_deadline: a fresh operation creates one absolute deadline before claim; claim, final revalidation, start, and reconciliation share the same absolute deadline, every remote timeout hint is min(request_timeout_ms, remaining), and no remote call begins when remaining is zero
failure_policy.sealed_authority: before any provider read or write, accept only a module-private branded VerifiedSealedRelease capability minted after existing trusted-filesystem and sealed-custody validation, with the complete sorted path/hash/size inventory derived from verified bytes; ordinary objects, copied fields, symbols, prototypes, and serialized clones are not authority
failure_policy.last_known_good: before start, reload the provider active lifecycle identity through canonical sealed custody recovery and re-read both candidate and active LKG artifact bytes after all provider preflight reads; any custody, identity, path, size, or hash mismatch blocks start
failure_policy.rollback_identity_custody: rollback uses one canonical reversible lifecycle release ID binding the source manifest ID and new generation; later processes parse that ID, reload opaque sealed custody from the source manifest, and recompute the lifecycle digest exactly without a caller alias map or in-memory identity registry
failure_policy.rollback: Rollback approval binds candidate, expected active, and source release, but byte authority comes only from the opaque source capability. Both source candidate and active LKG are reloaded and byte-verified before the one-start mutation seam; every pending resume requires inProgress.expectedActive to equal the approval exactly before any operation poll or start and otherwise returns ROLLBACK_EXPECTED_ACTIVE_MISMATCH; exact replay revalidates custody and is an idempotent no-op.

readback.authentication: Use the job-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN/OIDC only for deployment. Any later operator read-back token must be least-privilege and supplied at runtime; no token is stored in this repository.
